steps.title: 10,000 devices behind eight feeders
steps.say: An invented aggregator's program in a hot summer territory: 10,000 enrolled homes, each with a smart thermostat, an EV charger, a home battery or rooftop solar, on eight distribution feeders. The registry says what each device is rated for; sixty days of feeder SCADA and portfolio meter data come with it, gaps and all, including eight past events on the hottest days. A second file of five devices is checked row by row: an unknown device kind, a 30 kW 'home' battery and a feeder that does not exist are refused, and the two good rows wait as commissioning until they have telemetry.

steps.title: What the telemetry says the devices will really do
steps.say: The availability models learn from the sixty days and the eight past events: how hard each air conditioner works at a given temperature, how much a setpoint raise cuts, how fast owners give up as the heat builds, how much load comes back afterwards, how often a car is plugged in, and for each battery its real capacity and the reserve its owner really keeps, which for one in six differs from the registry. Then tomorrow's forecast: a heat wave hotter than any day in the history, every feeder near or past its thermal limit at the evening peak.

steps.title: The utility calls 17:00-20:00; the bid and the plan
steps.say: The utility calls an event for the evening peak. The fleet's deliverable is drawn 300 times over what the forecast and the models can get wrong, and the bid is its 25th percentile, where one more megawatt's capacity payment equals its expected penalty. A bid at nameplate is refused by the policy check. The dispatch optimiser then decides which homes are curtailed for which hours, how hard each charger is throttled and which batteries discharge when, so the bid holds every fifteen minutes and no feeder goes over its limit when the air conditioners come back on.

steps.title: 18:15: feeder F4 goes dark
steps.say: The plan cannot keep two small feeders fully inside their limits at the forecast peak, so it will not run until a person accepts that. At 16:45 every device gets its schedule for the evening. At 18:15 the gateway for feeder F4 drops: the cloud can no longer see or command its 1,476 devices. They keep running the schedule they were given and release on it, inside their own limits (batteries stop at their owner's reserve, thermostats let the owner give up). The cloud re-plans from what it can still see. Beside what ran: the same evening if the devices had reverted to normal when the link dropped, and with no outage.

body.review_note: F5 and F8 stay a fraction over at the forecast peak; their own devices cannot cover it. Accepted, utility informed.

steps.title: Settlement, and the audit trail
steps.say: The market settles on the portfolio meter against a 10-in-10 baseline with a day-of adjustment capped at 20%. On a heat wave that baseline is far below what the homes would really have used, so the fleet is credited with much less than it delivered. A weather regression and the simulation's own counterfactual are shown beside it; only the simulation knows the truth. Every step is in a hash-chained audit log.
